 Veterinary expert warns pet owners over infections during rainy season 
 By:
 ">
 -->
 By: CORRESPONDENT 
 | 
 3rd Nov 2026 
 | 
 3 min read
 Listen 
 NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 3 – Pet owners have been urged to keep their dogs and cats vaccinated and dewormed during the rainy season to protect them from infections and parasite infestations. 
 Rosebella Ochango, a veterinary professional and business developer at PetStore Kenya, said increased moisture, muddy conditions and flooding could expose pets to diseases such as leptospirosis, fungal infections, skin conditions and gastrointestinal illnesses.
 She warned that puppies and unvaccinated dogs were particularly vulnerable to serious infections such as parvovirus, as well as respiratory and gastrointestinal illnesses linked to exposure to infected animals, contaminated food and water, and poor sanitation.
 Ochango advised pet owners to maintain regular vaccination and parasite-control programmes under the guidance of qualified veterinary officers.
 She said owners buying dewormers and flea-and-tick treatments over the counter should follow product instructions and ensure the dosage is appropriate for their animals’ age and weight.

 “The product information states how often to apply each one (for example, monthly or every three months), so follow it carefully and check the dose against your pet’s weight and age,” Ochango said.
 “There are separate products for dogs and for cats, so always choose the one made for your pet’s species. Your vet is still the right person to guide you on how often to treat your pet,” she added.
 She also urged owners to keep vaccinations, including rabies, up to date and seek veterinary attention if their pets develop persistent itching, vomiting, diarrhoea, lethargy or loss of appetite.
 Proper hygiene is also important during the wet season. Ochango advised owners to clean pets’ sleeping areas regularly, dispose of animal waste promptly and keep feeding bowls and drinking water clean.
 She said mud and moisture could accumulate in animals’ coats, causing matting, skin irritation and infections if pets were not properly cleaned and dried.
 On nutrition, Ochango said healthy dogs and cats generally did not need changes to their diets during the rainy season. However, owners should store dry food in cool, dry places and discard any that shows signs of mould or contamination.
 She further advised owners to provide indoor activities to keep pets physically and mentally active when heavy rainfall limits outdoor exercise.
 The Kenya Meteorological Department has forecast above-average short rains in 44 to 47 counties through November and December 2026, increasing the need for pet owners to pay attention to preventive care.
 Ochango said PetStore Kenya’s role extended beyond supplying pet products to helping owners make informed decisions on nutrition, preventive care and animal welfare.
